title: an assignment whose value is the target itself destroys the old value before copying it
compiler: prints `del T 4`, `1`, `del T 0` in a default build and `del T 4`, `4`, `del T 4` with -O0: it destroys the old value of `o` and then copies it. `b = a and b` and `b = a or b` where `b` decides, and `a = a and b` where `a` decides, read the destroyed target the same way; `b = a or b` where `a` decides, and `h.u = h.t and h.u`, destroy the old target before the test at both levels
fixed: copies the value, then destroys the old one. As the pin does for any other target, the old value dies at its last use: for a fresh target that comes before the expression, through a call such as `b = pick(a, b)` it is the call, and when the target is an operand, it comes inside the expression, at the copy when the target decides, so the old value dies after it. It prints `del T 4`, `4`, `del T 4`; the human ruled the whole family a bug on 2026-11-21

confirmation.notes: provisional ruling, until the human has discussed it with Modular

nightly.result: prints the same as the pin at both levels for o = o, b = a and b, b = a or b and a = a and b; so do the nightlies 1.3.0.dev2026111705 and 1.3.0.dev2026112017, and Mojo 1.2.0 prints what the pin's default level prints for o = o, b = a and b and a = a and b
